result.reason: The mishna text presents the full case including Beit Shammai, Beit Hillel, and Rabbi Yehuda's statement together as one unit, and the 'Mishna Statement' heading is where the opening mishna of the perek is introduced and discussed, making it the natural home for the complete mishna text before the essay breaks down its components in subsequent sections.

The passage presents the gemara's question about why Beit Shammai rules the person is a nazir despite mentioning only figs (items foreign to nezirut), which is precisely the problem the 'Beis Shammai Problem' section describes — how a declaration mentioning only figs can create actual nezirut — before then giving Rabbi Meir's answer, which belongs to the next section.

The passage introduces Rabbi Yosi's principle that 'a person is held accountable for the conclusion of his statement' and the concept of 'neder upitcho imo,' which directly corresponds to the 'Rabbi Yosi Position' section (index 5) that describes Beit Hillel holding like Rabbi Yosi — the 'Neder Pitcho Imo' section (index 6) elaborates on the concept after it has been introduced.

The passage asks why Beit Shammai's case isn't also a 'neder upitcho imo' — a vow with its own inherent opening — which is precisely the concept being introduced and explained in the 'Neder Pitcho Imo' section's prose.

Both items explain the Gemara's resolution of the Beit Shammai/Beit Hillel dispute in Rabbi Natan's braita version — Beit Shammai following Rabbi Meir (person is nazir, then seeks dissolution) and Beit Hillel following Rabbi Shimon (statement is void as not donated in the manner of donors) — which is precisely what the 'Version 1' prose describes as the braita's different framing where everyone salvages the statement in some way.

The passage presents Rabbi Natan's baraita with Beit Shammai saying nadur ve'nazir and Beit Hillel saying nadur ve'ein nazir, which is exactly what candidate 1's prose describes as 'Version 1' of this dispute.

The passage presents the *lishana achrina* version of Rabbi Natan's baraita where Beit Shammai says nadur ve'eino nazir and Beit Hillel says lo nadur velo nazir, mapping to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon respectively — exactly what the 'Version 2' prose describes.

The passage is the actual mishna text listing the mincha variations (barley→wheat, flour→fine flour, without oil→with oil, half-issaron→full, one-and-a-half→two), which is precisely what the 'Mincha Variations' prose introduces and describes.

Both items together present Chizkiyah's identification of the tanna kamma with Beit Shammai (item 1) and Rabbi Yochanan's alternative reading that even Beit Hillel could agree (item 2), which is precisely what the 'Tanna Kamma ID' prose describes — Chizkiyah's position followed by Rabbi Yochanan's counter-reading of the same question.

All four items form a continuous chain about the gemara's challenge to Chizkiyah's position (lentils vs barley, the Beit Shammai parallel, Chizkiyah's retraction, Rava's explanation, and Rabbi Yochanan's counter), which is precisely what candidate 3 ('Gemara Challenge') discusses — the pressing of Chizkiyah's internal inconsistency via the Beit Shammai/grogros parallel.

Both items together present Rabbi Yochanan's 'dilma lo mibaya ka'amar' argument — the 'Reversal Theory' explaining why the mishna's use of se'orim rather than adashim does not force Chizkiyah to retract, because adashim could be read as an attempted chazara with tefos lashon rishon applying — which matches the 'Reversal Theory' prose precisely.
